label: GO after an unrewarded trial, early in the episode, leaning toward a1
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (100% of mass) and only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward == 0, 100% of mass); it never fires at D1 or D2 or after a rewarded trial. Within that, it is strongly concentrated early in the episode: rate 11x on trials 1-2, ~6x on trials 0-9, decaying to zero by trial ~50. It also prefers GO steps where the policy favours a1 (choice logit > 0: 87% of mass is model_act a1) and where S1 is good. GO & prev_reward==0 alone has recall 1.0 but precision 0.08. Adding ep_trial < 30 and choice > 0 (both observable, choice being the agent own policy) gives dev P 0.47 / R 0.68 / F1 0.56 / mass recall 0.83. Substituting the actual upcoming action a1 for choice > 0 gives the same F1. Precision stays incomplete: many early, unrewarded, a1-leaning GO steps are silent, and no simple history variable (previous transition, stay, reward pattern) separates them. The unit looks like an early-episode, a1-biased signal gated by lack of reward, not a clean model-based variable. Magnitude is largest in the top-choice / high-value bins (value 7.7-8.1), which I checked only through the mass tables.
